name: Grant Allen
bio: Grant Allen (1848–1899) was born near Kingston, Ontario, and made his career in England as a popular writer on natural science, a novelist and a journalist. He wrote verse only occasionally.
The poems given here are taken from The Oxford Book of Canadian Verse, chosen by Wilfred Campbell (Toronto: Oxford University Press, 1913).

poems.title: A Prayer
poems.author: Grant Allen
poems.collection: The Oxford Book of Canadian Verse (1913)
poems.text:
A crowned caprice is god of this world ;
On his stony breast are his white wings furled.
No ear to listen, no eye to see,
No heart to feel for a man hath he.
But his pitiless arm is swift to smite ;
And his mute lips utter one word of might,
'Mid the clash of gentler souls and rougher,
‘Wrong must thou do, or wrong must suffer.'
Then grant, O dumb, blind god, at least that we
Rather the sufferers than the doers be.
